profile.name: Gladys Muthoni Ndungu

profile.headline: RLHF & LLM Red Teaming
profile.tagline: I help large language models reason accurately about math, finance and code, and I write down exactly why an answer is wrong.
summary: AI evaluation specialist and Stanford PhD in Computational Finance who helps large language models (LLMs) reason accurately about math, finance and code.

Has authored 120+ expert benchmark problems with partial-credit rubrics, evaluated 2,000+ model responses for reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) and supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reached >95% inter-rater agreement on safety and policy scoring.

Equally strong on generalist evaluation: careful reading, strict guideline adherence and clear written explanations of exactly why an answer is wrong. Backed by 6+ years of production machine learning, quantitative risk modeling and Python engineering.
profile.availability: Open to AI training and evaluation roles

experience.role: Senior AI Evaluation Specialist & Full-Stack Engineer
highlights: Authored 120+ expert-level benchmark problems in derivatives pricing, stochastic calculus, econometrics and probability, each with a verified step-by-step solution and partial-credit rubric, now used in production RLHF training sets.
Evaluated and annotated 2,000+ LLM responses in finance, data science and software engineering for numerical accuracy and reasoning quality; written justifications are used directly as SFT data.

Built a taxonomy of 15+ recurring failure patterns found while debugging model-generated Python, SQL and JavaScript (sign errors in Greeks, mixed compounding conventions), cutting reviewer adjudication time ~20%.

Red-teamed and scored sensitive financial-advice prompts against safety guidelines over 3 calibration rounds, reaching >95% inter-rater agreement on policy adherence, misleading guidance and over-refusal.

Checked each response for factual accuracy, instruction-following, logical coherence, completeness and policy adherence, and wrote clear, guideline-based explanations of exactly where and why it failed.
Peer-reviewed 60+ expert benchmark submissions for mathematical correctness, answer uniqueness and rubric clarity before publication.

Built the team's grading tools (Elixir/Phoenix, PostgreSQL, Redis, React) handling 5,000+ API requests per minute at p99 latency under 120 ms, with role-based access control that passed a security audit with zero critical findings.
Architected a multi-factor equity risk engine across 3,000 US tickers, delivering daily volatility and drawdown attribution to 50+ registered investment advisors.
Deployed a churn-prediction microservice with automated MLflow retraining, increasing retention conversion by 15% and saving ~$400K in annual revenue.
Raised test coverage from 40% to 85% with automated model-validation checks on every pull request, and cut time to detect data drift across 6 production models from 48 hours to under 2.
Researched neural-network and gradient-boosting models for credit default prediction and covariance estimators for high-dimensional portfolios; awarded Best Student Paper.
Explained complex quantitative topics to 120+ students in Investments and Python for Data Science, supervised 8 master's dissertations, and maintained a backtesting library used by 12 PhD students.
Built PD/LGD credit risk models for 800+ corporate bond issuers, reducing manual analyst overrides by 22%.
Automated performance attribution in Python and Snowflake SQL, cutting the monthly reporting cycle from 72 hours to under 4.
Designed Airflow pipelines with automated data-quality checks (99.7% reliability over 14 months) and stress-tested $2B+ multi-asset portfolios.
Built a GARCH volatility forecasting module and a vectorized derivatives backtester (under 0.1% P&L deviation from historical execution).

projects.name: quantprice
projects.summary: Options-pricing library that doubles as a generator of verified ground-truth problems for evaluating LLM mathematical reasoning.
highlights: Black-Scholes-Merton prices and Greeks, CRR binomial trees (European and American), Monte Carlo with antithetic and control variates, barrier, lookback and geometric Asian options, and implied volatility (Newton with Brent fallback).
Benchmark generator for 11 topics with a JSONL schema, tolerance bands and worked solutions, plus a grader that reports accuracy by topic and difficulty; a 330-problem dataset is committed.
Every benchmark answer is re-derived by independent code (50-digit mpmath, a plain-loop tree, root finding); the largest disagreement measured is 3.4e-9 of the grading band.
Cross-validated against QuantLib, and every formula cites its source; the README lists what the library does not handle.

projects.name: eval-studio
projects.summary: Web app for scoring LLM responses against weighted rubrics, comparing responses side by side and exporting the results.
highlights: Rubric scoring: each criterion scored 1-5 with a required written justification, issue flags for hallucination, policy and refusal, and a weighted score.
Side-by-side comparison with randomised, unlabelled left/right order to reduce position bias, a five-point preference with reasoning, and optional rubric scoring of both sides.
JSON and CSV export with protection against spreadsheet formula injection; a mock model by default, with optional Claude responses through the Anthropic API.
Tested with pytest, Vitest and a Playwright browser walkthrough; the Docker setup is built, health-checked and exercised end to end in CI.
